key: The Master said, ‘Not so. He who offends against Heaven has none to whom he can pray.’
s: Asked by Wang-sun Chia about a proverb preferring the furnace to the south-west corner, the Master rejects it; Zhu Xi, on 3.13, reads Heaven as principle: no prayer to corner or furnace clears one who defies it, so one should follow principle and court neither.
src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 3.13, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, Lunyu jizhu juan 2), revision 2063643 (2021)

opened.edition: zh.wikisource 四書章句集註/論語集注卷二, revision 2063643
opened.locator: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, commentary on 3.13 (子曰：不然，獲罪於天，無所禱也)

evidence.words: 天，即理也；其尊無對，非奧竈之可比也。逆理，則獲罪於天矣，豈媚於奧竈所能禱而免乎？言但當順理，非特不當媚竈，亦不可媚於奧也。
evidence.gloss: Heaven is principle itself; its honour has no equal, and the corner and the furnace cannot be compared with it. To go against principle is to offend against Heaven: how could flattering the corner or the furnace pray one free of that? He means one should simply follow principle: not only should one not flatter the furnace, one may not flatter the corner either.

reason: Problem holds on both counts. Legge's 3.13 proverb (day.js) sets the furnace against the south-west corner, so the plain sense now names both and the reading's 'corner or furnace' has its referent. Zhu Xi's 言但當順理，非特不當媚竈，亦不可媚於奧也 is a general rule, so the close now reads 'so one should follow principle and court neither' rather than pinning it on the offender; 逆理 ... 豈媚於奧竈所能禱而免乎 carries 'no prayer to corner or furnace clears one who defies it'; 天，即理也 carries Heaven as principle. Commentator, place, key, ref, at and src unchanged. Plain sense shares no four words with the key. verse.js ok (Analects 3.13, at 52); entry-check ok.
